vocabulary: Nouns – a lion, the harp, a wall, a giant, everything, a bear
grammarNotes: In this lesson, we’ll talk about ABILITIES. In the Bible there’s a special man with some special abilities. Look at the pictures. Who’s that?
Well, this character is David! David has abilities with instruments and he’s very strong! Now read the text.
I’m David. I can kill a lion and a bear. I can play the harp. I can climb a wall. I can kill a giant. I can do everything through the Lord!
Now from memory, don’t look at the text again and match the verb phrases.
And the answers are
climb a wall
kill a lion, kill a bear, kill a giant,
do everything
play the harp
Look at the sentences from the text.
I can kill a bear and a lion.
I can play the harp.
I can climb a wall.
I can kill a giant.
I can do everything through the Lord.
Look at the word CAN. This is a verb. It expresses ABILITY. David has these abilities. Equivale ao verbs PODER, ou SABER FAZER ou CONSEGUIR FAZER em português.
David can play the harp. = David sabe tocar harpa.
CAN is a special verb in English – a MODAL verb. Modal verbs are different from the other verbs.
The verb CAN doesn’t change.
I can play the harp.
David can play the harp.
Christine can play the harp.
You can play the guitar.
We can play instruments.
They can play the piano.
Another characteristic is that after the verb CAN, you always use another verb.

items.prompt: What can you do in God’s kingdom with your abilities?

grammarNotes: What can you do in God’s kingdom?
In this lesson, you’ll learn how to ask questions with the verb CAN.
A local church wants to invite people to serve in church. They ask them to fill out a form and answer some questions. The name of the form is “What can you do in God’s kingdom?”
Suppose you want to serve in that church with your talents, skills and abilities.
Read.
What can you do in God’s kingdom?
Answer these questions and find out how you can help in church.
Can you...
...sing?	...teach? ...speak in public? ...dance? ...play instruments? ...draw?
Do you like to...?
...pray? ...help people? ...talk about the gospel? ...study the Bible?
...lead people? ...organize parties?
You can…

...be a teacher. ...be a preacher. ...be a member of the worship group....be a counsellor....be a member of a prayer group ...lead a Bible study group....be an evangelist ...help organize events....do social work ...make signs or posters for events.
After you answer the questions, give it to one of the leaders and tell them how you can serve in church.

Well, let’s look at the church form one more time and this time study the verb CAN again. Now it’s in a question. Read again and think: “What is the difference between the verb CAN in the affirmative form (Lesson 1) and now in the interrogative form?” For example:
Can you sing?
Can you dance?
Can you play instruments?
Well, here’s the difference.
I can sing. (affirmative form)
Can you sing? (interrogative form)
So, the difference is like the verb to be. Invert the subject and the verb. Simple, huh?
Remember you use CAN with every person:
Can I sing? Yes, you can.
Can you dance? No, I can’t.
Can he speak English? No, he can’t.
Can she draw? Yes, she can.
Can they play instruments? No, they can’t.
And the short answers are with CAN.
Can you sing? Yes, I can. / No, I can’t.
Let’s practice that. Listen to the questions. Answer about you with
Yes, I can or No, I can’t.
With Wh-questions, the wh-word comes first.
For example,
What can you do in God’s kingdom?
What can David do?
What sports can Americans play?
What songs can John play on the piano?
Speaking of that (e por falar nisso), let’s answer the questions from the church form.
Se você disse Sim para aquelas perguntinhas do formulário da igreja, here is what you can do in God’s kingdom.
Can you sing? You can be a member of the worship group.
Can you teach? You can be a teacher in church. You can lead a Bible study group.
Can you speak in public? You can be a preacher.
Can you dance? You can be a member of the worship group.
Can you play instruments? You can be a member of the worship group.
Can you draw? You can make signs or posters for the church events.
Now that you know you can help in church with your abilities, talk to a leader and tell them you want to serve!
Now that you know the verb CAN in the interrogative form, you can do more exercises on the platform! See you!

vocabulary: not at all – de jeito nenhum (verbo na negativa)
grammarNotes: In this lesson, we’ll learn about a different way to express ABILITIES. It is possible to express abilities with ADVERBS OF MANNER.
Adverbs, ou seja, advérbios, são palavras que dão mais informações sobre os verbos, expressando como, onde, quando, com que frequência acontecem aquelas ações dos verbos.

No Book 1 vimos adverbos de tempo e de frequência (every day, once a week, etc, remember?). Nessa lição veremos advérbios de MODO, ou seja, ADVERBS OF MANNER. These adverbs express HOW you do an action.
For example,
David plays the harp well.
There are many Bible passages that describe David’s abilities with music and instruments. He’s the writer of 73 psalms, and the psalms are songs!
So, the expression WELL, describes how David plays the harp.
You can express ABILITIES in English with the verb in the simple present – we studied that in Book 1, remember? –  and then the adverbs of manner.
David plays the harp well.
Here are some adverbs of manner:
Examples:
You use adverbs of manner at the end of a sentence.
David plays the harp well.
Adverbs of manner usually end in -ly:
But there are some exceptions:
You can also use VERY, SO or REALLY before adverbs as an intensifier.
Juan sings very well.
You drive really carefully.
Turtles move so slowly!
Here are more sentences with adverbs of manner.
I sing well, but my father sings badly.
He swims fast, but she swims slowly.
She drives carefully, but her husband drives carelessly.
My brother speaks English a little, but my sister doesn´t speak at all.

vocabulary: (?) Can you draw? – Interrogative – yes-no question
(?) What can you do? – Interrogative – Wh-question
grammarNotes: Do you remember Moses? God speaks to him at the burning bush. He gives Moses a task (uma tarefa), a mission (uma missão). What does Moses answer? Read the text and say what Moses’s answer is.
God: Moses, go to Pharaoh and bring my people, the Israelites, out of Egypt
Moses: Oh, Lord, but I can’t speak very well.
What does Moses answer?
Yes, I can go, Lord.
Lord, I can’t speak very well.
No, I can’t go, Lord.
The answer is b. Moses thinks he has no speaking abilities. He has a speaking problem.
Look at Moses’s answer.  “Oh, Lord, but I can’t speak very well.”
What does “CAN’T” mean?
Well, CAN’T is the negative form of CAN. It is the contraction of CAN + NOT. It’s informal and for speaking. It means “no ability”, ou seja, “não saber”, “não ser capaz de fazer alguma coisa”:
I can’t speak very well. = Não sei / não consigo falar muito bem.
The formal verb is CANNOT:
I cannot speak very well. – for formal writing
Let’s summarize.
(+) David can play the harp.  – affirmative form
(SA) Yes, I can. / No, I can’t.  – short answers
(-) Moses can’t speak (very well).  – negative form

dialogues: A: Can you play any instruments?
B: Yes, I can play the harp.
grammarNotes: Let’s learn more about the verb CAN.

The name of this lesson is “Jews can’t work on Saturdays”. The Old Testament is about the history of the Jewish people. Today they have some specific rules. Read the text about that from Compton´s Interactive Encyclopaedia.
JEWISH TRADITIONS
The Jewish people are the descendants of Abraham. In their culture and religion, they have a lot of rules – things they cannot do and things they have to do.

The synagogue – It is the place where Jews can study the Scriptures and worship the Lord. The services take place on Friday evenings (the beginning of the Sabbath – the seventh day), on Saturday mornings and on Sunday afternoons. The rabbi (teacher) cannot be single – they have to have a family – wife and children. In the temple, men have to wear a “kipah” and women have to wear a veil. Men and women cannot sit together.

Rituals – The life of an individual and the family is marked by a series of rituals. Boys have to be circumcised when they are eight days old. When boys are thirteen, they have to participate in a ceremony called “Bar Mitzvah”, when they have to read from the Torah in front of the synagogue. Girls can do it, too, but they do not have to. Jews cannot work on Saturdays, because they observe the law of Moses, which says that the seventh day is a day of rest and worship.

Food – Food is very important for Jews. They cannot eat pork and they cannot cook food with blood. At Passover, they cannot eat regular bread, but they eat some bread called “matza”. Every Friday they say prayers and give thanks to God for their food in a special ceremony.
Now read the text again. Find 6 sentences in the text.
Six things Jews can’t do
Five things they have to do
And the answers are:
Six things Jews can’t (or cannot) do
1. The rabbi (teacher) cannot be single.
2. In the synagogue men and women cannot sit together.
3. Jews cannot work on Saturdays.
4. They cannot eat pork.
5. They cannot cook food with blood.
6. At Passover, they cannot eat regular bread.
Five things they have to do:
1. The rabbi has to have a family.
2. In the temple men have to wear a “kipah”
3. Women have to wear a veil in the temple.
4. Boys have to be circumcised.
5. Boys have to participate in a ceremony called “Bar Mitzvah”.
Look at the answers from the reading exercise. What verbs express prohibition? And obligation? CANNOT or HAVE TO?
CANNOT (or CAN’T) in this case expresses PROHIBITION.
They can’t work on Saturdays.
HAVE TO expresses OBLIGATION.
Men have to wear a “kipah”.
The rabbi (he) HAS to have a family.
Note: Kipah is this typical Jewish hat you see in this Picture.
Attention:
In the text, there’s a sentence with CAN:
They can study the Scriptures in the synagogue.
In this case, CAN doesn’t express ABILITY, as in Lessons 2 and 3. It expresses PERMISSION.
Modal verbs can have 2 or 3 meanings, or more!
How do you know the difference? By the context! For example,
Dialogue 1.
Dialogue 2.
Son: Mom, can I play my guitar now?
Mom: Finished your homework?
Son: Yes!
Mom: Yes, you can, dear.
In the first dialogue, CAN means ABILITY and in the second one, it means PERMISSION.
Remember the questions, “Can you repeat?” or “Can you spell your last name, please?”, the word CAN means REQUEST, ou seja, um pedido.
Summary

grammarNotes: Look at the Bible verses. What do they have in common?

John 15.5

Phillipians 4.13
Nothing is impossible with God.

If we ask anything according to God’s will, he hears us.”

The people are hungry. Give them something to eat.
Luke 8.16
What they have in common is the words EVERYTHING, SOMETHING, ANYTHING, AND NOTHING. These words are indefinite pronouns.

Remember the name of Lesson 1? “We can do everything through the Lord.” This is a Bible verse from the book of Phillipians Chapter 4, verse 13. Some versions say, “I can do ALL THINGS through Christ, who gives me strength.”
ALL THINGS = EVERYTHING (TODAS AS COISAS, TUDO)
Em português, esse versículo é: “Posso tudo naquele que me fortalece.”
Fala da nossa força em Cristo.
Attention that EVERYTHING and the other words are compound words.
EVERY + THING = toda coisa
Remember the words, SOME, ANY and NO from Book 1?
ANY + THING – ANYTHING –
alguma coisa (questions)
qualquer coisa (affirmative sentences) –
nada (negativa)

Jewish traditions
